rounds.text: Tiger Logistics is currently trading at a significant valuation discount compared to its sector peers, with a P/E ratio of 12.52x against a benchmark of 20.32x [E5] and a P/B ratio of 0.6x compared to the sector’s 1.54x [E6]. This suggests the market has overly penalized the stock, ignoring recent operational improvements where quarterly operating margins expanded to 5% in December 2020 from 3% in the year-ago quarter [E24]. The company is demonstrating early signs of a turnaround, evidenced by positive year-over-year profit growth exceeding 20% [E58] and sequential sales growth [E60]. Conceded: the company faces substantial headwinds, including a 0% three-year compounded sales growth [E13], a 48% decline in trailing twelve-month sales [E14], and negative ROA and ROE figures [E7, E8]. Despite these challenges, the current market capitalization of ₹ 269 Cr [E2] and the stock’s position near its 52-week low [E4] provide a compelling entry point for investors who believe the recent margin expansion [E24] and profit growth [E58] signal a sustainable recovery.

Tiger Logistics carries severe fundamental deterioration that is completely masked by superficial value arguments, as evidenced by a catastrophic collapse in top-line performance where 3-year compounded sales growth sits at 0% and trailing twelve-month sales growth plummeted by 48% [E13, E14]. This operational paralysis has driven operating margins down by 22 percentage points into negative territory at -16% in the TTM period compared to 6% three years prior [E23]. Consequently, profitability metrics are deeply distressed, featuring a return on equity of -21.01% and a return on assets of -13.11%, both underperforming sector benchmarks by wide margins [E7, E8]. Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 12.52x against a sector benchmark of 20.32x [E5] and displays a quarterly operating margin recovery to 5% in December 2020 alongside positive screen reasons for YoY profit growth and QoQ sales increases [E24, E58, E60].

The bear’s focus on trailing twelve-month metrics ignores the critical inflection point captured in the most recent quarterly data, which shows a significant operational turnaround [E24]. While the bear highlights a 48% decline in TTM sales [E14], it fails to account for the immediate momentum indicated by recent quarter-over-quarter sales growth [E60]. Conceded: the 3-year compounded sales growth is 0% and TTM operating margins are negative [E13, E23]. However, the bear’s characterization of "operational paralysis" is directly contradicted by the 2 percentage point improvement in quarterly operating margins to 5% [E24]. Furthermore, the market is currently mispricing the company’s recovery potential, as evidenced by a P/B ratio of 0.6x compared to the sector benchmark of 1.54x [E6]. By fixating on historical TTM distress, the bear overlooks the positive YoY profit growth signal that confirms the company is already executing a successful pivot [E58].

The bull’s reliance on a single quarter of margin improvement [E24] ignores the broader reality of a business in deep structural decline, as evidenced by a 48% collapse in TTM sales [E14] and 0% compounded sales growth over three years [E13]. While the bull cites a 5% quarterly operating margin [E24], this remains an outlier against the TTM operating margin of -16% [E23], suggesting that the company is still struggling to achieve sustainable profitability. Conceded: the company shows a 2 percentage point improvement in quarterly operating margins [E24] and YoY profit growth [E58]. However, these minor gains are dwarfed by the company’s severe underperformance in efficiency, with an ROA of -13.11% and an ROE of -21.01% [E7, E8]. The bull’s attempt to use a 0.6x P/B ratio [E6] to suggest value is contradicted by the company’s own filed statements, which show a P/B of 7.26x [E1]. Furthermore, the market’s skepticism is reflected in the stock price sitting at only 8% of its 52-week range [E4], indicating that investors are not buying the narrative of a turnaround.
